verdict.rationale: Intel's own product page documents an on-chip Xe Media Engine for playing, streaming and editing at once, which is the product's own media hardware for this story. However, it lists no specific codecs and is general Core Ultra family marketing rather than a 285K-specific spec. missing for 10: documented AV1 encode/decode support, HEVC encode/decode support, any ProRes-class support, a 285K-specific media engine spec, independent or hands-on corroboration of encode/decode performance.

support.subject: As a creator, hardware media engines carry my editing and streaming — documented hardware encode and decode (AV1, HEVC, ProRes-class) on the chip itself

citations.quote: Play, stream, and edit, all at once. Intel Xe Media Engine delivers sharp, high-def video without compromising game graphics.
you get the speed to game, stream and edit media with crisp visuals
